newsitem.title: UK: British water firms face early price review.
newsitem.headline: British water firms face early price review.

text.p: Water industry regulator Ofwat said on Tuesday it plans to review the price limits for all the 29 regional water and sewage firms in England and Wales in 1999 -- five years earlier than originally planned.
Ofwat set the current price limits in 1994 for a 10-year period, but said it feels it cannot wait until 2004 to let customers share in efficiency gains made by the firms.
"A gap of 10 years between reviews is too long, even given the long-term nature of the water industry," the regulator said.
His announcement for a 1999 price review follows strong criticism by the main opposition Labour Party alleging that Ofwat was too lenient on the water companies.
Critics argue that many of the water companies spend too much money on dividends for shareholders at the expense of properly maintaining their pipeline networks.

"The 1995 and 1996 droughts showed that companies need to give more attention to leakage control and maintaining a satisfactory balance between suppply and demand," said Ofwat's director general, Ian Byatt, said.
"This will be a major consideration at the next review," he added.
Ofwat will also look for ways in which customers in particular can benefit from the cost cutting drives at water companies in recent years.
"Customers have seen prices rising for too long," Byatt said.
Ofwat, which wants to see the 1999 review implemented on April 1, 2000, will publish a "periodic review" schedule early next year.
